endorsements.quote: Zu jedem Zeitpunkt unterliegt die Verantwortung der Diagnostik, Diagnosestellung und Therapie, auch bei Verwendung KI-gestützter Systeme, den behandelnden Ärzten.
Akteure sind in der Pflicht, die Verantwortung eindeutig zuzuweisen [ 32 ].
Der Überführung diagnostischer KI-Algorithmen zur Analyse radiologischer Bildgebung in die klinische Routine sollen externe Validierungsstudien vorausgehen [ 79 – 82 ].

Diese Validierungsstudien müssen robuste Referenzstandards [ 79 – 82 , 85 – 87 ] nutzen, auf „Confounder“ [ 88 – 92 ] prüfen und an realen Patientenkohorten [ 80 , 83 , 84 ] durchgeführt werden, um systematische Fehler zu vermeiden [ 92 ].
Um klinische Risiken durch den Einsatz von KI zu minimieren, sollten prospektive Studien durchgeführt werden, die auch klinische Endpunkte einbeziehen.
Der klinische Einsatz von KI zur Qualitätssicherung und Verbesserung der Patientensicherheit in der Chirurgie erfordert die zunehmende Einbeziehung aller Interessensgruppen.

unlisted_practices: Provide AI outputs to clinicians with understandable explanations and uncertainty estimates rather than simplistic yes/no answers, so outputs can be audited and communicated to patients.
Make AI tools interpretable and transparent, with plausible rationales consistent with medical knowledge.
Continuously update and validate machine learning models used to predict adverse drug reactions.
Consider federated learning to preserve data privacy while enabling robust multi-institutional models.
Integrate AI and digital health competencies into medical education and continuing training.
Develop federal-level uniform policy measures and legal frameworks for cross-institution and cross-state data sharing for AI.
Design AI health solutions multidisciplinarily from the outset, including ethics and legal experts, patient representatives, and industry.
Ensure patients can understand decision-support systems in basic terms to enable informed consent.
Ensure data security and data protection, including encryption, when implementing patient-facing AI chatbots, and integrate them into existing care structures.
Do not let AI fully replace the participatory physician-led informed consent conversation.
Deploy validated patient-education AI systems only under physician supervision.
Standardize clinical processes and documentation across institutions to enable AI development and data interoperability.
Consider ethical, moral, and cultural aspects in clinical AI implementation.
Measures to minimize negative impacts of radiological diagnostic algorithms should be taken, potentially institution-specific.

screen.reason: Delphi expert consensus statement discussing clinical application, barriers, and practice-oriented proposals for implementing AI in surgical disciplines.
